12.t: Working with data: smoking and lung function
q: What is the lung function of a 65-year-old who never smoked?
Compare the lung function of a smoker and a non-smoker at 65.
Non-smoker 82%, smoker 48%: the smoker is 34 percentage points lower.
What happens to lung function after a person stops smoking at 45?
It still falls, but slowly, at the same rate as a non-smoker; lost function does not come back.
Use the data to argue why stopping early matters.
Damage builds up over time and is not reversed; stopping earlier keeps the curve higher, so the person is less likely to reach the level where they are disabled by breathlessness.
